Also have you got an internal playbook for handling these so we can align our runbooks?

Hi Laura —

Thanks for flagging — this is an important area. High-level summary up front, followed by proposed contract wording and the playbook we use internally.

Summary (short):
- Redwood responds to valid legal process (subpoena, court order) in the jurisdiction where the request is issued.
- We will notify the customer of requests that relate to their account unless: (i) we are legally prohibited from doing so (e.g., a nondisclosure/order from the issuing authority); or (ii) notice would materially impede an active investigation (we escalate to our Legal team for case-by-case determinations).
- Practically, we aim to provide preliminary notification to customers within 24–72 hours of receipt where no legal prohibition exists; a final confirmation (what was produced) follows after review and redaction checks.

Why 24–72h?
- 24h: target for high-severity or customer-impacting requests when we can safely confirm (no gag order).
- 72h: reasonable window for triage, legal review, and ensuring we do not contravene law enforcement instructions. This aligns with many enterprise expectations while preserving legal safeguards.

Proposed clause (suggested as a DPA addendum):
"Redwood shall, to the extent permitted by applicable law, notify Customer promptly and, in any event, within seventy-two (72) hours of receiving a lawful request for Customer Data from law enforcement authorities. If Redwood is prohibited from notifying Customer by a binding legal order or statute, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide Customer with notice as soon as such prohibition is lifted. Redwood will cooperate with Customer's reasonable, documented requests to contest or limit disclosure, provided Customer reimburses Redwood's reasonable legal costs associated with such efforts."

Internal playbook (brief):
1) Intake & triage (0–4 hours): Security ops logs request; Legal opens matter; confirm jurisdiction and scope.
2) Legal review (4–24 hours): Determine validity, gag orders, and whether notice is permitted.
3) Customer notification (24–72 hours): If permitted, send preliminary notice with high-level scope and contact.
4) Production (24–120 hours): Collect, review, redact, and produce responsive records with chain-of-custody notes.
5) Post-production: Confirm to customer what was produced and offer support for any follow-up.

I've attached a one-page playbook and a proposed redline for the DPA clause. Happy to iterate.

Best,
Mina Haddad

Mina / Rishi —

This is great. A couple of pragmatic notes from Product/CS angle that we should bake into the playbook and clause:
- Include an explicit statement that Redwood will not proactively search for non-customer data beyond scoped requests (limits disclosure to Customer Data defined in the DPA).
- Add a short sample customer notice template (we should be able to automate that in the Console to speed the 24–72h notice).
- For enterprise customers that require immediate escalation, include an SLA-like opt-in: e.g., "Customer may opt into an emergency-notify workflow (1 business hour response) under a paid support addendum."

Sample notice template (one-liner to include in clause appendix):
"Redwood has received a lawful request for Customer Data related to your account. Redwood does not believe the request requires immediate action by Customer; Redwood will provide an update within seventy-two (72) hours and will cooperate with Customer to the extent permitted by law."

If this looks good I can add the automation tasks to the roadmap and draft the Console message schema.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Solutions

Team —

Agree with the language. A few legal clarifications to propose before we send to Acme Legal:
- Replace "seventy-two (72) hours" with "prompt notice, and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours where not prohibited by law" to preserve flexibility.
- Add a short sentence that Redwood may require reimbursement of reasonable legal costs when customer asks Redwood to actively contest or seek modifications of a law enforcement request on the customer's behalf. (We should be transparent; customers often expect this).
- Confirm cross-border considerations: if the request originates from a jurisdiction that Redwood cannot legally comply with (conflict of law), Legal will notify Customer and propose alternatives (e.g., request sent to customer for local process).

I'll produce a redline later today and recommend Legal Ops run a quick SLA/Notification automation feasibility with Product.

Rishi Malhotra
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Laura / John —

Thanks for the question. Per Rishi and Marissa's input above, attached is a redlined clause and a short internal playbook that summarizes the intake, legal review, notification windows, and production steps. Key takeaways:
- We will notify customers promptly unless prohibited by law; target window is 24–72 hours for preliminary notice when permitted.
- We will limit disclosures to Customer Data as defined in the DPA and will not perform broad searches beyond scope.
- If a customer requests Redwood to actively challenge a lawful request, we will consider doing so but may require reimbursement of reasonable legal fees.

Please review the attachments and let me know if Acme Legal wants alternative wording for the reimbursement sentence or the emergency-notify opt-in. We can schedule a quick 30-minute sync if preferred.
